disclaimer: Nutrient charts are starting points, not guarantees. Water quality, crop load, temperature, media, and plant response can change the right strength. Follow product labels and measure carefully.

hydropip.label: HydroPip timed-feed towers
hydropip.summary: Open, timed-feed perlite-vermiculite towers with no runoff return to the reservoir.
hydropip.operation: Mix one complete fresh batch, let the level gradually fall, and select the next strength when the reservoir is nearly empty.

dwc.label: DWC / raft
dwc.summary: Roots remain in an aerated nutrient solution.
dwc.operation: Monitor water temperature, aeration, pH, and EC because roots are continuously exposed to the solution.

nft.label: NFT
nft.summary: A thin, recirculating nutrient film continuously passes the roots.
nft.operation: Keep flow uninterrupted and monitor pH and EC because a small root-zone volume can change quickly.

drip.label: Drip / drain-to-waste
drip.summary: Nutrient solution is delivered through emitters and is not returned to the reservoir.
drip.operation: Use runoff and media moisture to tune feed volume; verify each emitter before changing nutrient strength.

recirculating_drip.label: Recirculating drip / Dutch bucket
recirculating_drip.summary: Drip-fed containers return solution to a shared reservoir.
recirculating_drip.operation: Monitor pH and EC because returned solution changes the reservoir over time.

ebb_flow.label: Ebb and flow
ebb_flow.summary: The root zone is periodically flooded from a recirculating reservoir.
ebb_flow.operation: Check reservoir strength, flood coverage, drainage, and root-zone oxygen between cycles.

kratky.label: Kratky / passive
kratky.summary: A non-circulating reservoir supplies the crop as the level falls.
kratky.operation: Start conservatively, preserve the air gap, and avoid disturbing established roots with aggressive corrections.

aeroponic.label: Aeroponic
aeroponic.summary: Roots receive nutrient solution as a fine spray or mist.
aeroponic.operation: Protect nozzles from precipitation, keep backup irrigation available, and monitor pH and EC closely.

other.label: Other hydroponic system
other.summary: A custom or less common hydroponic setup.
other.operation: Use the nutrient label as the source of truth, then verify the result against plant response and measured pH/EC.

mixed.label: Mixed garden
mixed.note: Use the dominant crop and the most sensitive plants to choose a conservative target.

lettuce.label: Lettuce
lettuce.note: Leafy crops usually need less strength than mature fruiting crops.

basil.label: Basil
basil.note: Watch heat and flowering before assuming a flavor or leaf problem is nutrient related.

spinach.label: Spinach
spinach.note: Keep solution temperature and oxygen in mind when growth slows.

parsley.label: Parsley
parsley.note: Establishment can be slow, so choose stage from true growth rather than age alone.

tomato.label: Tomato
tomato.note: Demand rises substantially as flowering and fruit load increase.

pepper.label: Pepper
pepper.note: Increase cautiously and use plant response because pepper sensitivity varies.

cucumber.label: Cucumber
cucumber.note: Large plants can consume water quickly; do not confuse falling water level with a need for a full nutrient dose.

strawberry.label: Strawberry
strawberry.note: Use a crop-specific program when precision is important and watch fruiting-stage demand.

other.label: Another crop
other.note: This broad range is only a starting point. Confirm a crop-specific target before making large adjustments.

unknown_tap.label: Tap / well water, not tested
unknown_tap.note: The starting water contributes minerals and alkalinity. Test its pH and EC before mixing when possible.

soft.label: Soft or low-mineral water
soft.note: Low-mineral water gives a cleaner baseline, but some programs may need calcium and magnesium support.

ro.label: RO / purified water
ro.note: Use a nutrient program intended for low-mineral water and verify calcium and magnesium are supplied.

hard.label: Hard / high-alkalinity water
hard.note: High alkalinity can push pH upward. A water test or hard-water nutrient program is worth using before repeated correction.

rain.label: Filtered rainwater
rain.note: Screen debris and avoid contaminated roof runoff; measure the starting pH and EC before mixing.

hydropip_masterblend.label: HydroPip MasterBlend batch
hydropip_masterblend.bestFor: The real HydroPip timed-feed tower system and growers who want a simple month-scale batch method.
mixingOrder: Fill the reservoir with fresh water and start the internal mixing pump.
Add magnesium sulfate and let it dissolve.
Add calcium nitrate separately after the other ingredients are dissolved.
Circulate until evenly blended, then verify tower flow.

seedling.label: Seeds and young seedlings
seedling.reason: A light HydroPip starting batch for germination and small seedlings.

vegetative.label: Established vegetative growth
vegetative.reason: The normal HydroPip batch once sprouts have several true leaves and are actively growing.

fruiting.label: Heavy growth and fruit production
fruiting.reason: The HydroPip production batch for mature plants and a substantial flowering or fruiting crop load.

masterblend_label.label: MasterBlend 4-18-38 label rate
masterblend_label.bestFor: Growers using the manufacturer program in DWC, NFT, drip, Kratky, or another reservoir size.
mixingOrder: Dissolve MasterBlend 4-18-38 in the reservoir water.
Add magnesium sulfate and dissolve completely.
Add calcium nitrate last and mix thoroughly.
Never combine calcium nitrate with the other products as a concentrated premix.

seedling.label: Initial growth / seedlings
seedling.reason: The manufacturer directs growers to use half rate until seedlings are well established.

vegetative.label: Established growth
vegetative.reason: The full manufacturer label rate after seedlings are well established.

fruiting.label: Flowering / fruiting
fruiting.reason: The manufacturer full rate is the baseline; use crop-specific EC and plant response to refine it.

jacks_321.label: Jack's 3-2-1
jacks_321.bestFor: Established plants in recirculating or drain-to-waste hydroponic systems using a simple dry three-part program.

unsupportedStages.seedling: Jack's recommends a dedicated clone formula for young seedlings before moving to a base program. Use the product schedule or choose Custom label rate for the exact product in hand.

mixingOrder: Add Jack's Part A (5-12-26) and dissolve completely.
Add magnesium sulfate and dissolve completely.
Add Jack's Part B (calcium nitrate) last.
Mix thoroughly, then check pH and EC after the solution stabilizes.

vegetative.label: Established vegetative growth
vegetative.reason: Jack's published 3-2-1 base formula for established plants.

fruiting.label: Flowering / fruiting baseline
fruiting.reason: Use the published 3-2-1 base as a starting point and refine with the crop-specific Jack's schedule when higher precision is needed.

gh_flora_3part.label: General Hydroponics FloraSeries 3-part
gh_flora_3part.bestFor: Growers who prefer liquid measuring and stage-specific control in DWC, NFT, drip, ebb-and-flow, or soilless media.
gh_flora_3part.sourceLabel: General Hydroponics FloraSeries 3-Part General Use feed program
mixingOrder: Add FloraMicro to fresh water first and mix well.
Check EC, then adjust pH after the complete solution is mixed.

seedling.label: Seedling / clone
seedling.reason: The General Use seedling rate from the current FloraSeries 3-Part program.

early_vegetative.label: Early vegetative growth
early_vegetative.reason: The first established-growth step in the General Use program.

vegetative.label: Late vegetative growth
vegetative.reason: The late-growth General Use rate before flowering or fruit set.

flowering.label: Early flowering
flowering.reason: The General Use transition rate as flowering begins.

fruiting.label: Mid flowering / fruit production
fruiting.reason: The General Use mid-bloom rate for active flowering and fruit set.

ripening.label: Ripening / late production
ripening.reason: The General Use ripening rate as nitrogen demand tapers.
